construction_notes: Default is defined as being at least 60 days late with payments on the loan at the end of the year; an individual is in default if they have at least one delinquent loan at the end of the year.

About 5% of the adult population is in financial trouble in any given year; 5% of the children and 6% of the parents are recorded as having defaulted on unsecured loan payments during the data period (Table 1).
All amounts in Table 1 are in 2011-DKK; a dummy variable is denoted by (d).

In the unemployment event study all amounts are index-adjusted to 2009-DKK by computing x_{y,c,i} * xbar_{2009,c} / xbar_{y,c}, where x_{y,c,i} is the original amount for individual i in cohort c observed in year y.

Severity variants of the default definition restrict delinquency to loans with balances exceeding DKK10,000, DKK50,000 and DKK100,000; the default loan level may reflect defaults on several smaller loans adding up to the defined amount.

The behavioural instrument is the within-parental-cohort decile of the ratio of average financial assets to average disposable income for the parents over each of the years 1987-96; financial wealth is the sum of stocks, bonds and bank deposits.
Income vigintiles/deciles and GPA deciles are constructed separately for each cohort.
The ex ante interest rate on a specific loan in 2004 is computed as interest payments during the year divided by nominal debt at the end of the year.

The low financial wealth indicator equals one if financial assets at the end of the year are less than one month's worth of the individual's average disposable income in the five years preceding the shock year.

An unemployment shock is an unemployment spell of at least three months in event year 2007, 2008 or 2009, for individuals employed and without unemployment spells in the five preceding years; the control group is reweighted to account for age asymmetries and to give each shock year the same weight.
The exchange rate has been in the range of 5-6 DKK per USD in the period from 2004 to 2011.
